title: 2023 Bum Bowl
dek: The inaugural Bum Bowl, a two-week total over NFL weeks 15 and 16 of 2023, in which Araleasers (Ramon) routed Ben Dover (Sonny) 187.5 to 104.7 and sent Sonny to the first last-place finish in Buckaroo Football League history.
body: The 2023 Bum Bowl was the last-place game of the Buckaroo Football League's first season. The six-team league settled its basement through a consolation ladder, and this matchup decided who finished sixth of six. While Habibsters (Kaushal) were winning Buckaroo Bowl I, the league's two worst regular-season teams played for the right not to be the answer to a trivia question.

Ben Dover (Sonny) entered as the 5 seed after a 6-8 regular season with 1,413.3 points. Araleasers (Ramon) entered as the 6 seed at 4-10 with 1,375.3 points, the league's worst record. With the title already out of reach for both, the only thing left to play for was the avoidance of permanent embarrassment.

On paper the regular season favored Sonny completely. Ben Dover swept all three meetings: 102.64 to 79.14 in week 1, a 82.94 to 80.64 squeaker in week 6, and 121.98 to 114.8 in week 11. Neither manager had a title to his name, which in the league's first year was true of everyone.

The bottom two seeds were sent to the consolation ladder, and the league's records show that Ramon and Sonny had already met there once in the 2023 postseason. Ramon won that game 184.3 to 163.1, his first victory over Sonny after three regular-season losses. The records kept for that game do not include individual player scoring, so who carried each side there is not documented.

That result reversed the season series at the worst possible moment for Ben Dover. Sonny had beaten Brucie three times when it counted for seeding and then lost to him when it counted for survival. The rematch, a two-week total across NFL weeks 15 and 16, would decide sixth place.

No play-by-play exists for this game; the league website did not begin saving in-game events until week 7 of 2026. The order of scoring within each week is therefore not recorded, and only weekly totals survive.

Week 15: Araleasers took a 72.7 to 61.1 lead. Jahmyr Gibbs led Ramon's side with 23.8 points, supported by James Conner (16.4), CeeDee Lamb (15.1) and Justin Tucker (12). Ramon did so with real holes in the lineup: Chris Olave was held to 0, the Cowboys D/ST finished at -1, and neither Keenan Allen nor Kirk Cousins scored. For Ben Dover, Davante Adams posted 20.1 and Alvin Kamara 13.5, but Saquon Barkley managed just 4.7 and Garrett Wilson 4.4, while Terry McLaurin's 23.1 sat on the bench.

Week 16: The second week turned an 11.6-point lead into a blowout. Araleasers scored 114.8, the same number Ramon had lost with to Sonny in week 11, as Lamb (22.2), Gibbs (22), Conner (19.7), Olave (18.8), Kittle (16.1) and Tucker (16) all reached double figures. Ben Dover managed 43.6, its lowest weekly total of the postseason, with Barkley's 17.9 the only meaningful contribution; Adams scored 0.9 and Harrison Butker 1. Meanwhile Breece Hall scored 37.1 on Sonny's bench, nearly matching the entire starting lineup's week by himself.
The final was 187.5 to 104.7, a margin of 82.8 points. Ramon outscored Sonny in both weeks, and the second-week gap alone, 71.2 points, would have been enough to decide it.

Jahmyr Gibbs was the game's best player, scoring 45.8 points over the two weeks against a projection of 26.1. He had averaged 11.2 points a start in 14 regular-season starts, and he roughly doubled that in each week of the Bum Bowl. James Conner was the biggest surprise: 36.1 points against a 24.4 projection after averaging just 6 points a start across 12 starts. CeeDee Lamb added 37.3, slightly above his 35.7 projection, and Justin Tucker kicked in 28 points against a projection of 17 and a season average of 8.2.

Ben Dover's lineup came up short nearly across the board. Alvin Kamara scored 19.5 against a 29.9 projection after averaging 17.4 a start; Saquon Barkley scored 22.6 against 30.3; Garrett Wilson 15.7 against 25; and the Packers D/ST produced 1 point against a projection of 11.2, a choice that sat awkwardly with a Chicago manager. Davante Adams' 20.1 in week 15 was followed by 0.9 in week 16.

Both managers started players who were projected for zero and scored zero: Keenan Allen and Kirk Cousins for Araleasers, Josh Jacobs and Justin Herbert for Ben Dover. That left both teams without a scoring quarterback. Ramon had Trevor Lawrence (24 points) on the bench; Sonny had Patrick Mahomes (32.4).

Sonny's bench outscored his starters, 163.3 to 104.7. Mahomes in for Herbert, Hall (39.4) in for Jacobs and McLaurin (29.6) in for Wilson would have added 85.7 points, more than the 82.8-point margin, although Ramon's own bench held 119.6 points, including Lawrence, Derrick Henry (23.9) and Khalil Herbert (20.3), that could have answered.

Sonny finished sixth of six, the first last-place finish in league history, and Ramon finished fifth. Ben Dover had more regular-season points and a 3-0 regular-season record against Araleasers, yet lost both postseason meetings by a combined 103.9 points.

The result began one of the league's defining arcs. Ben Dover finished last again in 2024, making Sonny the only manager with two last-place finishes, before going 13-3 in 2025 and winning Buckaroo Bowl III. The 2023 Bum Bowl is now remembered as the bottom of a worst-to-first story, and the bench that would have saved him remains part of the evidence.

For Ramon, the Bum Bowl was the high point of a 4-10 debut season. Two years later he was removed from the league for inactivity after week 8 of 2025, and he now runs No Banner only HULK, a far better team than the one that needed a two-week blowout to escape the basement.
